### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 09e07c259a633eb02fdb29bedfe911e808529f88` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d3fc5b71d82c6bb0e1610c089fdf1e989f9ce316` — the merge of head `8e9e7d48fc79bf28989970391209dd0299045d6a` into base `09e07c259a633eb02fdb29bedfe911e808529f88`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d3fc5b71d82c6bb0e1610c089fdf1e989f9ce316 && git checkout d3fc5b71d82c6bb0e1610c089fdf1e989f9ce316
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 09e07c259a633eb02fdb29bedfe911e808529f88 8e9e7d48fc79bf28989970391209dd0299045d6a && git checkout -B drift-repro 09e07c259a633eb02fdb29bedfe911e808529f88 && git merge --no-ff 8e9e7d48fc79bf28989970391209dd0299045d6a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 09e07c259a633eb02fdb29bedfe911e808529f88
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `83ff895f4b65351f139a482ef598626b27e2df72`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.test.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-localization-cache.test.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-localization-fallback-organization.pin.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints-localization.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.test.ts + .changeset/25248-localization-fallback-organization-scope.md (judged under ②), packages/core/src/security/system-write-organization.ts on `origin/main` (`resolveSystemWriteOrganization` :109-125, the D9 predicate), packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts on `origin/main` (`callerOrganizationIdOf` :141-143, `organizationReachOf` :1867-1877, `organizationWallStands` :1890-1895, `withinReach` :2976-2981, `loadScopedRows` :3006-3044 — the #25226 reach this fallback mirrors), packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service-plugin.ts on `origin/main` (:334-345 the `tenancyPosture` and `organization` wiring; :499-506 "not the requested posture"), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/tenancy-service.ts (:109-137, the posture in force against the requested one), packages/types/src/env.ts (:147-164 `resolveTenancyPosture`), the four production callers — packages/core/src/security/request-execution-context.ts :274, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts :730-749, packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts :662-675, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts :376-392 — docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md D8 :663-696 and D9 :698-734, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs (the question the `Clause-②:` value answers), scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs :185-191 (how `yes (narrowing)` is faced), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (`judgeLevel` :1715 ff.), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (:746-752 and the operand grammar :1196), AGENTS.md :1084-1093.

Inputs read: card #25248 body, its claim (`6350248910`) and the os-dev-report (`6353098105`); the #25226 record `6343868210` (③ 3a, this card's origin); the PR body, file list and its one comment (the docs-drift bot); `net.diff` (7 files, +313/−36 against `09e07c25`); the 43 check-runs staged on the head; the head copies and ADR-0131 in the brief's folder. Every cited file was read by ref (`83ff895f` or `origin/main`), never from a working tree. The head is a merge of `origin/main` (`09e07c25`) into the dev's last commit `417fe64988`; the seven files are byte-identical between the two, and main's 12 commits since the dev's measurement base `1eb1afae07` touch none of the cited files.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. Which `sys_setting` rows the fallback now reads, per posture and caller shape.** `localizationFallbackReach` (head :2489-2508) is asked before the direct read (:2583) and its answer is applied twice: in the query (`organization_id` in the `where`, :2597-2602) and in memory (`settingRowOrganizationOf(r) === organization_id`, :2609), the two-sided rule `preferredRow` / `withinReach` gives the settings service. Per shape:
- a caller naming organization X, under every posture: `own(X)` (:2497) — `organization_id = X`, nothing else. Same as `organizationReachOf` :1868-1869, which also takes `''` as none (`callerOrganizationIdOf` :141-143).
- naming none, requested posture `single`, D9 derives X: `own(X)` (:2499-2500) through `resolveGuestOrganization` (:1276-1296), the same predicate the settings plugin wires as its `organization` source (plugin :344-345) and the engine asks on a system insert. The organization-less `America/New_York` row beside it is not read (pin :127-134).
- naming none, `single`, zero or several organizations: `refuse` (`no-organization` / `ambiguous-organization`, predicate :121, :125) → `unowned` (:2507) → no query at all (:2593; pins :136-148 assert `settingQueries` empty). The service does the same (`organizationReachOf` :1876, `loadScopedRows` :3012).
- naming none behind a requested wall (`group` / `isolated`): the predicate refuses `walled-posture` before any probe (:115-116) → `unowned` → no query, even at one organization (pins :150-156). A walled caller naming its own organization still reads it (pins :158-162).
- naming none, the organization read failing: `tryFind` throws `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` for anything but an unprovisioned table (:440-441); the `catch` at :2502-2506 turns it into `unowned` — nothing read on a guess, no memo written (pin :165-175, `settingQueries` empty). An unprovisioned `sys_organization` table is zero organizations (:440) → `refuse` → `unowned`: the same answer by a different route.
- no `sys_organization` registered (lean embedding, #25133 letter A): `no-organization-object` (:2501) → `organization_id: null` in the `where` and `=== null` in memory, so the rows written with no organization and only those (pin :178-187, `[null]`).
**Right in every row of the table**, and it is the reach #25226 gave the service (`withinReach` :2976-2981), so the fallback can never answer a row the service it stands in for would refuse — see 3 for the one direction in which it answers less.

**2. No cross-organization read remains.** Before (merge-base :2537-2545 as #25226 read it): `scope: 'tenant'`, no organization, first row per key, `limit: 10`. After: the organization is in the query and compared again in memory; the `$in` over the three keys bounds `own` at three rows; the success cache (:2447-2456) can only hold a scoped answer. The two-organization fixture lists the OTHER organization's row first (pin :76-79) so a positional pick would be caught; the filter-dropping engine (pin :110-118) catches a reach trusted to the filter alone; the organization with no row of its own gets the built-in, not a neighbour's (pin :105-108); a NULL row is not an organization's fallback (pin :120-123). **Right.** The dev's real-engine probe (`isolated`, `org_a` reads `org_b`'s `Asia/Tokyo` on `main`) is the leak the card named; it is not committed, and nothing here depends on it.

**3. The posture input.** The fallback reads the REQUESTED posture (`resolveTenancyPosture()`, env :147-164), as this file's platform-standing anchor does (:1617-1624); the settings service reads the posture IN FORCE off the `tenancy` service (plugin :337, :499-506). The two differ only when a wall was requested and the deployment runs degraded (`OS_ALLOW_DEGRADED_TENANCY=1`): the posture in force is the requested one or `single` and nothing else (`tenancy-service.ts` :109-137). In that one case the fallback reads nothing for a caller naming none where the service would derive — the fail-stricter direction, the direction the anchor already takes, and it costs only an organization-less caller's localization on a degraded wall while the settings service is also failing. **Right**, and the fallback is never wider than the service (3a in ③ records it as the residual it is).

**4. No legitimate read is lost.**
- Lean embedding: kept (1, last row). One edge: a lean composition whose environment nonetheless requests a wall reads nothing, because D9's predicate refuses `walled-posture` before asking whether an organization object exists (:115-122). The engine's write side has the same order, so no organization-less row can be written there through the engine; nothing exists to lose. **Right.**
- A fresh `single` boot: zero organizations → built-ins (R1 measured: `me/localization` 200, `UTC` / `en-US`); after the first sign-up a signed-in user names its active organization (`request-execution-context.ts` :274, `authz.tenantId`) → `own`; a signed-in user holding none → the one derived organization. **Right.**
- An 18.0-born store: both fixture rows are owned (#25226 record, fixture :665-666) → `own`; the dev reports the harness 16/16 and the `18.x upgrade harness (opt-in)` lane is in progress on this head (one earlier run `skipped` before the label, the #25226 pattern). A v17 store under `single` has its rows attributed by the D10 ceremony before boot; under a wall they stay NULL and answer nobody — exactly what #25226 ruled for the service, and the changeset's remedy names the ceremony. **Right.**
- `group`: `own(X)` alone, as the service reads under `group` (#25226 ① 1). **Right.**

**5. Callers.** All four production callers hand a vetted organization: `request-execution-context.ts` :274 (`authz.tenantId`); `current-user-endpoints.ts` :733-742 (the request's execution context, `me/localization`); `mcp/plugin.ts` :669-674 (`initial.tenantId` of the resolved entry); `audit-plugin.ts` :376-388 (the row's organization, undefined for an organization-less record — which now derives under `single` and reads nothing under a wall, the plugin's own D9 comment at :390-392). Nothing client-supplied reaches `tenantId`. **Right.**

**6. The failure memo.** A failed derivation does not populate the memo (:2502-2506): the memo exists for the DIRECT `sys_setting` read throwing (:2025-2042, #11877), and the derivation is not that read. `backendFailed` is still set only inside the direct read's `catch` (:2610-2613). **Right.** Observation, no action: core's `resolveGuestOrganization` carries no memo (#25226 ③ 4 said so), so on the #10221 environment a caller naming none now repeats a failing `sys_organization` probe where it used to repeat a memoized `sys_setting` one; on a real engine the success cache (seams + TTL, :2447-2456) bounds it to one per TTL per key, since `unowned` returns a cacheable success. The success key is `tenantId|userId` (:2413) and `LOCALIZATION_CACHE_WATCHED_OBJECTS` is `sys_setting` / `sys_platform_setting` (:2155), so a derived answer for a caller naming none survives a second organization's creation for at most the TTL, on the failing-service path only. Bounded; noted in ③.

**7. Scope, not retire — sound.** Retiring would drop what #10221's memo is keyed on and the bind-window answer (#11580's re-resolve replaces a value, not a built-in), and would leave `plugin-audit`'s and `mcp`'s organization-less readers on built-ins whenever the service is unbound. Scoping makes the fallback a strict subset of the service's reach (1-3). The cost is a second copy of the reach rule (core :2489-2508 beside service :1867-1877 / :2976-2981); `@objectstack/service-settings` depends on `@objectstack/core`, so the one predicate D8 asks for would have to live in core — a follow-up, not this card's (③ 3b).

**8. Tests edited beside the pins.** The fixture rows gain the caller's organization and nothing else: `makeCountingQl` (:178-199) reads an absent column as NULL and refuses combinators; the cache test's `t1` / `t2` case asserts read counts only (:166-176), so `t1` reading no `o1` row leaves it exact; plugin-hono-server's rows carry `ORG = 'org_lang'` (:54) and the session's `activeOrganizationId` is the same `ORG` (:166); the runtime fixture's key carries `active_organization_id: ORG` and that file's own pin (:139-152) is what makes it the `tenantId`. The new pin's double applies the `where`, refuses every combinator, implements `$in` alone, honours `limit` and toggles `registry.getObject` for the lean case (:26-65). **Right.** The ablation (A1 12/14, A2 1/14, A3 2/14, A4 1/14) is the dev's measurement, not re-run here; each red set names the pin that owns the arm, which is the shape the card's acceptance asks for.

**9. Gate verdicts on the head** (43 runs): 13 `success` — Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Check PR Size, Auto Label, filter, Flag docs affected by code changes, Check Documentation Links, the claim check, the part-of check, the single-writer-path check and the same-issue check; 10 `skipped` (event- or path-filtered, the dogfood shards and Dogfood Verify CLI among them, as on #25226); 20 `in_progress` — Test Core 1-6, Build Core, Check Changeset (twice), the four Type Check lanes, seven Lint lanes, the 18.x upgrade harness; **0 failures**. The dev reports all 41 runs green on `417fe64988`, whose seven files this head carries unchanged; the seat confirms the 20 on this head before posting. `check-governed-merges --branch`: 0 of 7 paths governed, not Tier H/S.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/25248-localization-fallback-organization-scope.md`: `'@objectstack/core': patch`; summary `fix(core)!: …`; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; `Metadata-protocol: none`; the `**BREAKING**` banner; FROM / TO and the remedy; the adr-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its why. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines, bare and line-initial.

- **Level — right.** Under the house rule (AGENTS.md :1091-1093; `judgeLevel`) the level follows the metadata-protocol kind alone: `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner and ADR-0087 disposition. The diff changes which stored row a degraded read takes; no authorable key, value, type, default or meaning changes, so `none` is the right kind and `patch` the right level. Both carriers are present.
- **ADR-0087 marker — right.** `no-migration-prescription` is honest: nothing exported is removed or renamed (`resolveLocalizationContext` keeps its signature), the remedy is an operator data action (the ownership ceremony, re-saving each value inside its organization). Mechanically safe: the `FROM:` / `TO:` bullets carry no arrow, and `Setup → Localization` has no code-ish operand on either side (operand grammar :1196: a backticked span or a dotted/slashed path), the same shape #25226's `Setup → the settings page` passed on.
- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` — the value is wrong; `no (narrowing)` is right.** The value answers one question (clause2-line.mjs): does this card widen an accept set or expand the public surface. This diff widens nothing: `ResolveLocalizationInput` and the module's export set are unchanged; `localizationFallbackReach` and `settingRowOrganizationOf` are module-private; no new env var, no new accepted shape, no new error, no new route. The one new demand on `ql` — a `null` comparand honoured as IS NULL — tightens what a `ql` must do, it does not widen. The dev's reason ("follows #25226's declaration for the same narrowing") misreads that record: #25226's `yes` was earned by `bindEngine`'s new optional `organization` input (its ② paragraph says so in those words), and this diff carries no such widening. The arm `(narrowing)` is right: an accepted read input stops answering. Face and level are unaffected either way — `yes (narrowing)` already routes to the narrowing face (record-recognisers :187-188) and `judgeLevel` reads the kind — so the correction is gate-neutral: the value on the changeset's line 7 and on the PR body becomes `no`, and nothing else in either carrier changes.
- **Who is affected / remedy** match the measurement: a healthy service never reaches the read; only a store holding organization-less tenant localization rows, or an organization with no row of its own, sees a different answer while the service fails.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Dev flag — `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` (shallow) and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (no build) exited 3 locally, 0 after unshallow / build.** Answered: the Lint and Build lanes that run them are in progress on this head with 0 failures so far; the dev reports them green on `417fe64988`, identical in these files. The seat confirms.
2. **Dev flag — `@objectstack/organizations` added to the showcase locally for R4, then restored.** Answered: the file list is the seven files and no manifest; nothing of it is in the diff. That a walled `os serve` of the showcase refuses without the package is pre-existing and not this card's.
3. **`open_questions: []`** — nothing to answer. Three observations the dev did not list, none blocking:
   - **a.** The posture divergence in ① 3: the fallback reads the requested posture, the service the one in force. Bounded to a requested wall running degraded, where the fallback is stricter. No action; recorded so the next reader of either rule knows they differ by design.
   - **b.** Two copies of the reach rule (① 7). A follow-up card under #15212's gate ③ could hoist `OrganizationReach` and `withinReach` into core beside `resolveSystemWriteOrganization`, so the service imports the one predicate D8 names. Not this card's surface.
   - **c.** The unmemoized `sys_organization` probe and the cache key without the derived organization (① 6): bounded by the success cache on a real engine and reachable only while the service fails. No action.
4. **`out_of_scope_findings` (a) — the PR body predates `417fe64988` and this merge head.** Answered: the body names a 6-file size, proof head `0139af1fe3`, and says no merge was taken; the head is a merge of `origin/main` into `417fe64988` (made 22:54Z, after the os-dev-report), 7 files, +313/−36. Judged the code, as the brief says; the seat may amend the body.
5. **`out_of_scope_findings` (b) — the `Clause-②` re-declaration to `yes (narrowing)`.** Not accepted — ② above. The claim said the dev re-declares from the diff, and the diff carries no widening to earn `yes`. This is the one item behind the verdict; the remedy is the value on both carriers.
6. **Deviation 1 — the first edit was made in the primary checkout through a python write the guard hook does not see; work then moved to a linked worktree, the primary left detached at `origin/main` and clean.** Escalated to the seat as a process matter: the committed tree is what this record judges and it is right; whether a guard bypass in the dev container needs a note of its own is the seat's call, not a code question.
7. **Deviation 2 — builds and package tests ran outside `os-verify-lock.sh`; only the dogfood battery ran under it, in a container with no other session.** Answered: the check-runs on the head are the gate; local runs are advisory, and the battery the lock exists for ran under it.
8. **CI still running when staged.** The verdict rests on the code and on what has completed (0 failures); the seat confirms Test Core, Build Core, Check Changeset, the Type Check and Lint lanes and the upgrade harness on `83ff895f` before posting, and this record does not stand if any of them fails.
